newsitem.title: USA: Dow Magnesium dismisses Hydro dumping view.
newsitem.headline: Dow Magnesium dismisses Hydro dumping view.

text.p: Dow Magnesium has dismissed suggestions made earlier this week by Norwegian rival Hydro Magnesium that it was dumping metal on the European Union market.
"We certainly don't believe we are dumping anywhere," Frank Petitti, Dow Magnesium's global business director said.
Dow sells a "fair quantity" of magnesium in Europe.

"If Norsk as saying there appears to be another anti-dumping movement, then that has to be on transaction prices, not necessarily on published prices, and I just don't know what those are," Petitti said.
In the past MagCorp successfully filed an anti-dumping suit against imports into the U.S. of Canadian pure magnesium. Hydro operates a large magnesium plant in Quebec.
Meanwhile, Petitti said it was too early to forecast how the market looked in 1997, and the industry was waiting for the next set of International Magnesium Association data.
"I think we saw 1996 as a little disappointing in volume," Petitti said. "But I think the market will come back."
He said the announcement this week by Queensland Metals Corp it was going ahead with its magnesium project, was unlikely to disrupt the market.
"They have studied the marketplace very well, and it will come on when, I believe, it will be needed," Petitti said.

Work on Queensland's pilot project, develped jointly with Normandy Mining Ltd and cash backing from Ford, will start in February, before moving to build a 90,000 tonnes per year commercial plant, starting in 12-18 months time.
